commit.message:
[BugFix][WeightTransfer] Align NPU IPC reload lifecycle and add the three-model IPC/HCCL state-transition cases (#16959)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Split out of #16355 (second of three PRs). Implements **Phase 0 —
Restore transaction parity** from RFC #16322.

The NPU IPC worker engine implemented `start_weight_update` and
`finish_weight_update` as `pass`, so unlike the HCCL engine it never
entered vLLM's layerwise reload: a packed or unpacked IPC transfer
handed weights to a live layer, and the checkpoint-facing / derived
state the transaction is supposed to restore was never refreshed.

Changes:

- `start_weight_update` now calls `initialize_layerwise_reload`,
`finish_weight_update` now calls `finalize_layerwise_reload`.
- Fix the indentation of `self.model.load_weights(weights)` in the
packed receive path: it was inside the per-chunk loop, so the layer was
reloaded once per chunk instead of once per transfer.
- Reorganise the state-transition E2E matrix into
`one_card/rlhf/state_transitions` (NPU IPC) and
`two_card/rlhf/state_transitions` (HCCL), and extend it to **three
reduced models** — Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-bf16 and GLM-5.1 —
in **both** IPC and HCCL lanes, packed and unpacked. The source
enumerates the served parameter name/shape set from a meta model and
generates deterministic fixed-random BF16 tensors on demand: no
checkpoint shards are downloaded and no second model copy is stored.
- `tests/ut/distributed/weight_transfer/test_npu_ipc_engine.py` pins the
two hooks at the unit level.
- `.github/workflows/scripts/estimated_times.yaml` is repointed at the
new lanes.

The legacy `two_card/test_hccl_weight_transfer.py` (Qwen3-0.6B, one
model, one configuration) is superseded by the new model-aware HCCL case
and is deleted. Its assertion that the served weights changed after the
broadcast is covered by the strictly stronger `baseline !=
dummy_signature` check of the new suite, which compares both generated
text and token log-probs for every case.

**Note on the diff size:** this PR also carries the DeepSeek-V4
attention-sink fix from the first PR of the split. It is a hard
prerequisite — without it the DeepSeek-V4 lane of the new suite fails
with "first live weight update does not match normal startup loading of
the same weights". The first PR should land first; the overlapping hunk
then rebases away to nothing.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. The NPU IPC live-weight-update path now performs the same START →
LOAD → FINISH transaction as HCCL.

### How was this patch tested?

- New/updated unit tests:
`tests/ut/distributed/weight_transfer/test_npu_ipc_engine.py` pins
`initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload`.
- New system tests:
`tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/rlhf/state_transitions/test_npu_ipc_weight_transfer.py`
and
`tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/rlhf/state_transitions/test_hccl_weight_transfer.py`;
each case starts from `--load-format dummy`, proves dummy inference in
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` mode, loads the complete fixed-random payload, and
requires an exact match after a pause/resume reload.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `py_compile` pass on all
changed Python files; all commits are DCO signed off.
- On hardware (from #16355, on the pre-split tree): two-card HCCL passes
Qwen3.5 and GLM-5.1 in both packed modes; one-card NPU IPC passes
Qwen3.5 and GLM-5.1 in both packed modes; DeepSeek-V4 required the sink
fix from the first PR. Hardware re-verification of this exact branch is
still pending, so please treat the e2e lanes as CI-verified only until
then.

Refs #16355, #16322.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

---------

Signed-off-by: Ronald1995 <ronaldautomobile@163.com>
Co-authored-by: Shaoxu Cheng <2906339855@qq.com>

commit.message:
[Feature] Enable GLM-5.3-flash PD disaggregation on Model Runner V1 (#16910)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Brings GLM-5.3-Flash prefetch/decode disaggregation to the default model
runner (MRV1) with the MooncakeConnectorV2 pull engine, reusing the
kernel-block layout prefract landed for MRV2 (#16755). Without this, PD
disaggregation only works with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1; the default
runner rejects the layout at KV init and the cross-TP handshake fails.

Three adaptation points:
- V1 reshape: two small-slot view branches mirrored from
_reshape_kv_cache_v2 – the per-request kpool tail ring packs a
contiguous suffix of the shared small slot, and the compressed indexer
packs natural kernel blocks as a contiguous prefix, each bounded to half
the slot.
- GLM-Next cache layout: size the shared small slot by the unified page.
_align_glm5_next_cache_specs derived the small page from the small
candidates only, so with MRV1's unpadded worker specs the slot collapsed
to the indexer's own page and the half-slot bound rejected the layout at
KV init. MRV2 workers pre-pad their specs, so their behavior is
unchanged.
- V1 reshape: expose the NOPE main as natural 128-row kernel blocks
instead of one page-sized block per scheduler block, so dim0 blocks stay
byte-identical across engines with different TP. The page-sized form
made the MooncakeConnectorV2 handshake reject cross-TP transfers with
different local and remote kernel block size 1152 | 640.

Depends on #16755.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No new flags, config options, or API changes. For users running
GLM-5.3-Flash with PD disaggregation on the default model runner,
cross-TP deployments (e.g. P=TP8 + D=DP2xTP4) now work out of the box.
All other models and colocated workloads are unaffected – branch
selection is identical to before (only GLM-Next publishes the stride
marker).

How was this patch tested?

On GLM-5.3-Flash w8a8 real hardware (TP8 single instance, P=TP8 + D=TP8,
and P=TP8 → D=DP2xTP4):
- Indexer and tail views bit-identical with the MRV2 reshape.
- Equal-TP full-verify passes (Serial + concurrent, all match; per-rank
ms-level pulls).
- Unequal-TP chain: handshake clean, three factual questions all
answered correctly, zero pull/transfer errors.
- TextVQA authoritative rescore (per-row gold alignment, post-
extraction): PD 92.0% identical to colocated 90.0% in the same batch.


- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

---------

Signed-off-by: sunbaosong <13793883820@163.com>

commit.message:
[MRV2][Test]Add DSpark probabilistic sampling E2E test (#16982)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds an end-to-end test for DSpark probabilistic speculative
decoding (`test_dspark_probabilistic_spec_decoding`) in Model Runner V2.
It verifies the probabilistic rejection sampling path, including
stochastic draft sampling, probability ratio tests, and residual
resampling. It also checks full-length outputs, cross-seed randomness,
and matches the acceptance rate against a golden baseline.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

This PR adds the `test_dspark_probabilistic_spec_decoding` E2E test,
which was verified on Ascend NPU.

commit.message:
[Doc][Model] Add Qwen3.8 Flash-Next deployment tutorial (#17024)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds a standalone deployment tutorial for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next to the
v0.26.0 release branch.

The tutorial:

- follows the existing Qwen3.5-27B/Qwen3.6-27B model-tutorial structure;
- documents the validated Atlas 800 A3-only, W8A8, DP1 x TP8 text
deployment;
- explicitly marks Automatic Prefix Caching as unavailable and requires
`--no-enable-prefix-caching`;
- includes the QSA Lightning Indexer and QSA Expand E3 enablement
switches;
- documents Function Calling with `--tool-call-parser qwen3_xml` and
reasoning parsing with `--reasoning-parser qwen3`, including tested curl
examples and thinking control;
- records the GPQA Diamond accuracy result of 90.4;
- intentionally omits performance results;
- adds the tutorial to MkDocs navigation and bilingual navigation-title
metadata.

This documentation describes the implementation in #15162, which
includes the Qwen3.8 model-support prerequisite, and also references
#16142 and #16995. #15162 currently carries an earlier copy of the same
tutorial; this standalone documentation PR is intended to supersede that
copy.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No code or runtime behavior changes. This is a documentation-only
update.

### How was this patch tested?

- `markdownlint-cli@0.45.0 --fix`
- `pre-commit run codespell --files ...`
- `pre-commit run typos --files ...`
- Ruff check and format for `docs/hooks/nav_titles.py`
- `git diff --check`
- Full `mkdocs build --strict`

commit.message:
[CI] Pin DeepSeek-V4 Flash GPQA nightly to low reasoning effort (#16721)

## Summary

- Pass the optional `reasoning_effort` benchmark setting through to
AISBench chat request generation.
- Set `reasoning_effort: low` for the DeepSeek-V4 Flash W8A8 A3 nightly
GPQA case. Keep `thinking: true` and the performance case unchanged.
- Add a focused test for the generated request config, including
unchanged behavior when the setting is absent.

## Context

The [failing nightly
job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/34497673764/job/103072819176#logs)
evaluated this case without an explicit reasoning effort. The
DeepSeek-V4 default thinking strength changed upstream, so this pins the
intended GPQA protocol rather than relying on that default.

An earlier manual GPQA Diamond run using `reasoning_effort="low"` and
`chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": True}` scored 88.38% (175/198) on the
e5118d15/vLLM 0.28.0 setup. That is supporting evidence, not a
validation of this PR's current-main nightly run.

## Validation

- Parsed the modified YAML and Python files; confirmed only the GPQA
benchmark selects `low`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- The new unit test and full A3 nightly GPQA run are pending CI/runner
execution.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

[Performance] Prioritize SAS metadata before QLI (#15949)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Refs #15280. Follow-up to #15443.

The metadata stream currently builds QLI metadata before SAS metadata.
An HCA-first model such as DeepSeek V4 Pro can therefore wait behind QLI
work that its first attention layer does not consume. SAS groups also
follow builder order, which may differ from their consumption order.

This PR changes `DeviceMetadataExecutor` to:

- Submit compressor tasks first, SAS tasks next, and QLI tasks last.
- Record each SAS group's first consumption in the existing `wait()`
path and reuse that order across subsequent batches. The first
submission retains the original SAS order; QLI is placed last
immediately.
- Validate the task-key set for FULL graphs while allowing producer
order to change. Per-group events, persistent buffers, and the existing
buffer-reuse fence are retained.

Runtime changes are confined to the executor.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or configuration change. This changes task ordering in the
existing asynchronous metadata path.

### How was this patch tested?

Validated rebased commit `61800b4c4`:

- **138 focused CPU unit tests passed**, covering executor ordering and
lifecycle, group-specific waits, graph task-set validation, DSA/DSA-CP
builders, compressor/indexer consumers, DSpark, and the model-runner
graph-event handoff.
- **4 real Ascend NPU tests passed**, covering both SAS consumption
orders in eager and FULL graph execution, capture without warmup,
producer reordering after capture, and repeated buffer reuse. The graph
cases perform 40 replays in total.
- `bash format.sh ci`: passed.
- Full `tools/mypy.sh 1 <version>` checks for Python **3.10, 3.11, and
3.12**: passed across `vllm_ascend`, `examples`, and `tests`.

CPU test command:

```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/ut/worker/test_device_metadata.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v1.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_cp.py \
  tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dspark_proposer.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_compressor.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_indexer.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py::TestDeviceMetadataFullGraphEvents
```

NPU test command:

```bash
pytest -q tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/aclgraph/test_device_metadata.py
```

End-to-end TPOT/throughput impact, including indexer-first workloads,
has not yet been measured.

commit.message:
[BugFix][P/D] Prevent decoder load double release after failed recompute (#16864)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #16517.

When a decode stream returns `stop_reason="recomputed"`,
`reassign_instances()` releases the previous decoder before assigning
replacement instances. If the retry prefill then fails or the client
cancels the request, assignment never returns and `generate_stream()`
still holds the previous `InstanceInfo`. Its final cleanup releases the
same decoder score again, making `active_tokens` negative and
permanently skewing the load-balancing heap.

This change tracks decoder release ownership on `InstanceInfo` and
routes reassignment through a release-once helper. Final request cleanup
skips the decoder decrement after ownership has already been released,
while still completing request accounting. This fixes the lifecycle at
its source instead of clamping negative scheduler scores.

The regression test covers both retry-prefill failure and
`asyncio.CancelledError`, asserting that decoder load returns to zero
and `request_num` is fully released.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or configuration change. The P/D load-balancing proxy now
preserves correct decoder load accounting when a recomputed retry fails
or is cancelled.

### How was this patch tested?

- Before the fix, the new regression test reproduced `active_tokens ==
-1000.0`.
- `python -m pytest -q tests/ut/proxy/test_load_balance_proxy_server.py
tests/ut/proxy/test_load_balance_proxy_scheduler.py`: 16 passed.
- Repeated the failure and cancellation ownership checks 100 times each:
200/200 passed.
- `bash format.sh ci`: all hooks passed.
- Real single-node 1P1D smoke test on two Ascend 910B3 NPUs with
Qwen3-0.6B and `MooncakeConnectorV1`:
  - non-streaming and streaming requests passed;
  - 10/10 sequential and 8/8 concurrent requests passed;
  - long-prompt and client-timeout cleanup passed;
- proxy `request_num` returned to zero and cards were released after
testing.

commit.message:
[Feature][Engram] Share host head shards across local DP replicas (#17134)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow up on #16925 with DP-shared Engram host storage. Replace CPU
owner sorting and variable all-to-all query routing with uniform head
shards. With sharing enabled, local DP replicas at the same TP position
map one physical host shard, query their own tokens, and retain only the
TP embedding all-gather.

Keep the repository's clean vLLM pin
`84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c` unchanged. Reuse its Engram
layout and hash-cache lifecycle, and selectively backport the required
V1 prompt lookback and uniform DP exchange from vLLM `f84b0c4bce` into
Ascend:

- Reuse the existing DP communicator under the single-node PP=PCP=DCP=1
boundary; no new communication group or distributed monkeypatch.
- Fill prompt-only V1 lookback through the runner override.
Generated-token history comes from the device slot cache, keeping async
draft placeholders out of history.
- Keep INT8/group32 FP32 scales, CANN HOST_UVA, the existing
rotated-checkpoint gate, and graph staging. Coordinate shared-table
loading, initialization failures and cleanup across DP ranks.
- Limit upstream monkeypatching to configuration parsing/resolution.
Also handle the empty-indexer sentinel needed during full decode graph
capture.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. The Ascend extension to `--engram-config` accepts:

```bash
--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"dp_shared_memory":true}'
```

`dp_shared_memory` defaults to `false`. Shared tables require co-located
DP replicas, a shared IPC namespace and enough `/dev/shm` capacity
(about 206 GiB for this checkpoint's two INT8 tables). Each rank
registers its mapping; the DP leader loads the corresponding TP head
shard and synchronizes with its peers.

Only uniform head sharding is supported. Private mode requires the head
count to be divisible by TP times local DP. **For the 24-head
checkpoint, TP2/DP8, TP4/DP4 and TP8/DP2 require
`dp_shared_memory=true`; those 16-rank private configurations are
rejected.** This changes the earlier row-sharded topology support. Row
sharding, nonuniform heads, V2, piecewise execution and new environment
variables are outside this PR.

### How was this patch tested?

Tested on A3 using a real INT8 DeepSeek V4.1 checkpoint and the
unchanged vLLM pin. Reference: unmodified vllm-ascend
`7f6c984b1204a3e2f11bf018f881193a6d7203b7` with the same checkpoint and
vLLM pin.

- **Unit tests:** 13 focused Engram/indexer tests passed, and the
existing model-runner V1 suite passed 70 tests (83 in the combined run).
They cover configuration/CLI, INT8 loading, HOST_UVA addressing,
shared/private routing, prompt lookback and the empty-indexer sentinel.
- **Distributed components:** shared TP2/DP8, TP4/DP4 and TP8/DP2, 16
ranks each, matched the CPU embedding oracle exactly for balanced, idle
and skewed token counts. TP4/DP2 private/shared outputs also matched
exactly. Shared lookup used TP all-gather without Engram DP collectives.
- **Numerical regression:** five teacher-forced samples, three repeats,
5,526 gold tokens / 16,578 aligned logprob values, exactly equal to
unmodified main (`max_abs_delta=0`). Prompt token IDs also matched. This
is a fixed-sample regression, not a full dataset accuracy claim.
- **Real P/D:** local P and a second A3 D, TP4/DP4, D with async
scheduling + DSpark(5) + FULL_DECODE_ONLY. All 17 requests passed,
including concurrency 8; all 896 output tokens had finite logprobs. Logs
confirmed actual KV transfer, and metrics confirmed draft/accept
execution. Full P/D request validation covers TP4/DP4; the other two
topologies have component validation.
- **Memory:** 16 ranks mapped the shared table at approximately 206 GiB
summed PSS with zero Private Dirty pages, so no per-DP physical copy;
shutdown checks found no remaining named Engram backings after a
graceful exit.

Paired cold-ID microbenchmarks used the same real weights and query IDs,
alternating A/B order. Direct gather-call medians were 97.3%-99.1% of
main. For the complete embedding path, including lookup and collectives,
the median of each iteration's slowest rank was:

| Tokens per DP | Main (ms) | Shared head (ms) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1.730 | 0.571 | 3.03x |
| 8 | 1.636 | 0.668 | 2.45x |
| 32 | 1.763 | 0.693 | 2.55x |
| 128 | 2.355 | 0.708 | 3.33x |
| 1024 | 3.115 | 1.202 | 2.59x |

The pipeline benchmark used the complete 384,006,168-row first-layer
table at TP4/DP4, eight warmups and twenty measured pairs. Every
compared BF16 output matched exactly. Hashing, gate and serving
scheduling were outside this benchmark. A single-node serving check,
differing from unmodified 7f6c984b only in the Engram flag, cuts
decoding step time by about 5% at low and moderate concurrency (roughly
6% at bs=1, 5% at bs=16) and shows no measurable change at large
4096/1024 batches, so the end-to-end gain stays in the single-digit
percent range rather than following the sub-path speedup.

commit.message:
[Performance] [DCP] optimize DCP decode streams and V-up projection (#16977)

What this PR does / why we need it?
Optimize the MLA DCP decode path to reduce dtype conversion and layout
transformation overhead:
- Remove explicit FP32 conversions of history attention output and LSE
before DCP packing.
- Run current-token FIA on a side stream, overlapping it with history
packing and communication on the main stream. Preserve event ordering
and tensor lifetimes across streams.
- Fuse V-up projection transposes and batch matrix multiplication with
torch_npu.npu_transpose_batchmatmul.
- Extend regression tests to cover stream ordering and BF16, FP16, and
FP32 history outputs.
Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
No API or configuration changes. This patch optimizes execution of the
existing MLA DCP decode path while preserving its intended computation.
How was this patch tested?
- Unit tests: All 27 tests in tests/ut/attention/test_mla_cp.py passed
in the Ascend container.
- Accuracy smoke test: Evaluated DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus W4A8 with
TP8/DCP8 on 100 GSM8K samples; raw evaluator accuracy was 95%.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

[Refactor][Ops] Remove unused vLLM quant lightning indexer (#17080)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The custom `vllm_quant_lightning_indexer` and its metadata operator no
longer have runtime call sites in vLLM Ascend. Their remaining
references were limited to their own implementations, Torch
registrations, build lists, and README examples.

This PR:

- removes the `vllm_quant_lightning_indexer` and
`vllm_quant_lightning_indexer_metadata` implementations;
- removes their PrivateUse1 and Meta bindings, schemas, and the
output-construction helper used only by this operator;
- removes their build entries for Ascend 910B, 910_93, and 950;
- retains the active `npu_lightning_indexer_quant` and
`npu_quant_lightning_indexer_v2` paths.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. The unused `torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_vllm_quant_lightning_indexer`
and `npu_vllm_quant_lightning_indexer_metadata` schemas are removed. No
vLLM Ascend runtime path uses these schemas, so normal inference
behavior is unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Static validation:

[Refactor][Ops] Remove unused vLLM quant lightning indexer (#17080)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The custom `vllm_quant_lightning_indexer` and its metadata operator no
longer have runtime call sites in vLLM Ascend. Their remaining
references were limited to their own implementations, Torch
registrations, build lists, and README examples.

This PR:

- removes the `vllm_quant_lightning_indexer` and
`vllm_quant_lightning_indexer_metadata` implementations;
- removes their PrivateUse1 and Meta bindings, schemas, and the
output-construction helper used only by this operator;
- removes their build entries for Ascend 910B, 910_93, and 950;
- retains the active `npu_lightning_indexer_quant` and
`npu_quant_lightning_indexer_v2` paths.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. The unused `torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_vllm_quant_lightning_indexer`
and `npu_vllm_quant_lightning_indexer_metadata` schemas are removed. No
vLLM Ascend runtime path uses these schemas, so normal inference
behavior is unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Static validation:

```bash
git grep -n -E 'vllm_quant_lightning_indexer|npu_vllm_quant_lightning_indexer|aclnnVllmQuantLightningIndexer|VllmQuantLightningIndexer'
# no matches

bash -n csrc/build_aclnn.sh
git diff HEAD^ --check
```

commit.message: [BugFix][SFA] Fix GLM5Next sparse MLA sinks and mask/window parameters (#16918) ### What this PR does / why we need it? GLM5Next's NoPE sparse MLA path on Ascend A5 traps inside `SparseFlashMla` under sustained load with data parallelism and ACL Graph enabled: ``` error code = 341 "The address for VEC to access UB is out of bounds" ``` The trap is probabilistic and only shows up after roughly a thousand requests at concurrency 128, which made it hard to attribute: AI Core errors are reported asynchronously, so the exception surfaces at an unrelated `synchronize()`, and the plog fills with `error code = 0` / "timeout or trap error" lines from the cores that were merely caught in the fallout. This PR fixes four defects on that path. Each is described with the operator source that governs it, from `cann/ops-transformer@master`. #### 1. `sinks` must be owned by the caller `SparseFlashMla` requires a per-head float32 `sinks` tensor (`op_host/checkers/sinks_checker.cpp:38`). Allocating one inside the adapter would leave it referenced only by the call's kwargs, so ACL Graph capture bakes in an address the allocator reuses as soon as the call returns, and replaying that graph reads freed memory. `SparseMLAMetadataState` now allocates it once, next to its other persistent operator buffers, and the adapter rejects calls that omit it. Also aligned with the operator's parameter checks: `cmp_mask_mode` must be 0 while `cmp_kv` is absent, and `ori_win_left` / `ori_win_right` must be -1 unless `ori_mask_mode` is 4 (`op_host/checkers/mask_checker.cpp:47,57`). A size check was added before the generated plan is copied into its fixed `[1024]` buffer, matching the operator's contract. #### 2. `ori_mask_mode` must be 0 in the sparse ori_kv scenario This is the one that causes the trap. On A5 the operator picks its template from which tensors are present, not from the mask mode, so passing `ori_sparse_indices` together with `ori_mask_mode=3` is accepted and still lands on the sparse template. What the mask mode changes is whether the kernel initialises its softmax accumulators (`op_kernel/arch35/sparse_flash_mla_swa_kernel_arch35.h:241`): ```cpp constInfo.needInit = 0; if (constInfo.oriMaskMode != 0) { for (bIdx...) { if (s1Size > s2Size || s1Size < expectQs) { constInfo.needInit = 1; break; } } } else { constInfo.needInit = 1; // mask mode 0 always initialises } ``` With mode 3 the condition is only met when some sequence has a query longer than its KV, which never happens on an ordinary decode step, so `needInit` stays 0 and the initialisation is skipped. A sparse gather does not write every accumulator slot, so the skipped slots keep whatever the previous step left in them; the vector unit then computes a UB offset from that residue and walks out of bounds. Mode 0 is also what the operator expects semantically: the selected indices are themselves the mask, since the indexer only offers causally valid tokens. The A2/A3 path enforces this explicitly (`op_host/sparse_flash_mla_tiling.cpp:542`), and the metadata interface ties the two together from the other side - with `ori_mask_mode=0` and a non-zero `ori_topk` it requires `ori_topk_length` (`sparse_flash_mla_metadata/op_host/sparse_flash_mla_metadata_check.h:447`). #### 3. The plan and the operator call described different work `SparseFlashMlaMetadata` produces the core-split plan, and the kernel walks the query rows according to it. The plan was generated during metadata construction, from the padded `cu_seqlens_q` and the full top-k length tensor, while eager and piecewise steps trim the query to the unpadded token count before calling the operator. Observed in practice: ``` query has 1 rows but ori_topk_length was planned over 418 rows (num_actual_tokens=1, num_input_tokens=418, cudagraph_mode=NONE) ``` The gap comes from data-parallel padding: a rank with one real token still runs the group-wide token count. The operator's TND contract requires the first dimension of `q` to equal the last element of `actual_seq_lengths_q`, which this breaks. The call now rebuilds the plan for the rows it is actually passing, with `cu_seqlens_q` clamped to match. A replayed full graph never reaches that branch, so the captured plan is left intact. Since the branch regenerates the plan anyway, it also takes the top-k lengths from the indices being passed rather than from the prediction made before the indexer ran - the sort leaves every `-1` at the tail of its row, so counting the non-negative entries gives exactly the left-aligned prefix the operator contract asks for (`sparse_flash_mla/README.md`, 约束说明), and unlike a prediction it cannot overshoot into the `-1` tail. #### 4. Two masks were bounded by the padded token count, so neither ever fired Both the top-k length mask in `SparseMLAMetadataState.prepare()` and the output mask in `sparse_mla()` compared against `query_start_loc[-1]`. The runner extends that terminator to `num_input_tokens` so the TND constraint holds, which makes it equal to the tensor length being masked - the masks were no-ops. The first one left padding rows claiming a top-k length derived from positions an earlier, larger batch had written, while their sequence lengths were zero. The second one was there to stop NaNs in unwritten graph-capacity rows from reaching the value and output projections, and never did. Both now use `num_actual_tokens`. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. ### How was this patch tested? Manually validated GLM5Next A5 sparse MLA inference with the updated parameters. Confirmed the previous sinks must be provided error no longer occurs. test on gsm8k: test on aime26: - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c --------- Signed-off-by: zzzzzz198 Co-authored-by: zzzzzz198

commit.message:
[BugFix][Kernel] Handle empty DSpark context after discard (#16636)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

A discarded asynchronous speculative decoding step can have zero valid
sampled tokens. With five draft tokens and one target token, all six
context entries are rejected and `valid_ctx_end` equals the request's
`ctx_start`. The DSpark input expansion kernel previously loaded
`target_positions[valid_ctx_end - 1]`, which reads before the tensor for
the first request or from the previous request for later batch rows. The
invalid position can propagate to RoPE and trigger an IndexCheck
failure.

Use the current request's first position as the safe anchor when no
valid context remains. Query positions then begin at that same position,
while the existing rejection and slot-mapping semantics remain
unchanged.

The regression test covers first-row underflow and cross-request reads,
both sampling modes, and int32/int64 position tensors.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API change. Discarded DSpark steps no longer cause invalid position
reads and NPU IndexCheck failures.

### How was this patch tested?

- `python -m ruff check vllm_ascend/ops/triton/spec_decode/utils.py
tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_copy_and_expand_dflash_dspark.py`
- `python -m compileall -q vllm_ascend/ops/triton/spec_decode/utils.py
tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_copy_and_expand_dflash_dspark.py`
- CPU boundary model for first-row underflow and cross-request reads
- Ascend NPU regression with the CI-pinned vLLM commit: 12 passed, 9
deselected
- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

commit.message:
[Feature][KVTransfer] Support DCP sharding for layerwise KV pool (#16498)

## What does this PR do / why do we need it?

Extends the layerwise KV pool (AscendStoreConnector, memcache GVA path)
to work correctly under **decode-context parallel (DCP)**. Without this
PR, enabling use_layerwise together with --decode-context-parallel-size
> 1 silently corrupts the pool:

1. **Dropped shards on save**: the plain `tp_rank % put_step` dedup
assumes all TP ranks hold identical KV. With DCP, ranks sharing
`(dcp_rank, head_or_tp_rank)` hold the same context shard while the
put_step groups span *different* shards - every non-zero DCP shard was
never written to the pool.
2. **Cross-shard overwrite in the shared region**: ranks sharing
`head_or_tp_rank` (`put_step > 1`, e.g. MLA) map the same region key,
and every shard wrote its local layout at region offset 0, overwriting
the other shards. Cached-hit generations then read
wrong-layer/wrong-shard data.

## Changes (`pool_worker.py`)

- `_is_layerwise_save_leader()`: exactly one rank per `(pcp, dcp,
head_or_tp)` group performs save/alloc; `DCP=1` keeps the previous
put_step semantics.
- `_global_group_alloc_size()`: with `put_step > 1` and `cp_scale > 1`
the region covers all shards (shard-major layout). The per-shard stride
is the group byte total aligned **up to the GVA hugepage size (2MB)** -
hybrid DSA groups (e.g. GLM-5.2 indexer entries every N layers) have
non-uniform per-layer bytes and a raw sum yields misaligned GVA
addresses that SDMA rejects (`-3102`).
- `_build_group_layer_builders()`: each shard's writes are based at
`shard_idx * shard_stride`. `put_step == 1` (GQA/MHA) ranks each own a
distinct region key and are deliberately left un-scaled.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No. DCP=1 behavior is bit-identical (leader rule falls back to the plain
put_step dedup; no region scaling).

## How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests: `tests/ut/kv_transfer/test_layerwise_dcp_sharding.py`
(leader rule across MLA/GQA rank layouts, region sizing, stride
alignment for non-uniform groups).
- E2E on 8x Ascend910B (A3):
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MLA), TP4 x DCP2 + memcache layerwise: cache hits
3328/3488 tokens; fresh vs cached-hit outputs identical across 3 runs
(previously cached hits returned corrupted output).
- GLM-5.2-w4a8 (DSA/MLA hybrid), TP8 x DCP8 + `enable_dsa_cp`: zero
`batch_copy` failures, 1024-token cache hits, stable cached-hit outputs
(needs `--enforce-eager`; graph-capture crash with DSA+DCP8 is a
separate known issue under investigation).

Depends on #16208 (PP global layer addressing) - stacked on its head
commit.

[Feature][SP] Enable MoE SP with DP=1 (#17061)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Upstream enables MoE sequence parallelism only when `data_parallel_size
> 1`.
However, Ascend FlashComm also supports the TP/EP, `DP=1` topology,
which
requires the same rank-local token sharding layout.

This PR adds an Ascend platform patch for
`ParallelConfig.use_sequence_parallel_moe`, preserving the upstream
all2all
backend, expert-parallel, and TP-size checks while removing only the `DP
> 1`
restriction.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. MoE models using a supported all2all backend can now enable
sequence
parallelism with `--data-parallel-size 1`, provided expert parallelism
is
enabled and `--tensor-parallel-size > 1`.

## How was this patch tested?

- Added unit coverage for:
  - DP=1 + TP>1 + EP + supported backend enables MoE SP.
  - DP>1 behavior remains enabled.
  - TP=1, EP disabled, and unsupported backend remain disabled.
- Passed static checks:
- `python -m ruff check
vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_parallel_config.py
tests/ut/test_platform.py`
- `python -m ruff format --check
vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_parallel_config.py
tests/ut/test_platform.py`
- `python -m compileall -q
vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_parallel_config.py
tests/ut/test_platform.py`

`pytest` was unavailable in the local Python environment, so the new
unit test was not executed locally.

commit.message:
[Feature][KVTransfer] Mooncake Layerwise KV Pool Support Pipeline parallel (#17183)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds Mooncake layerwise KV pool support for pipeline parallel
deployments.

The implementation:

- Binds backend-specific wire-key identity once and shares the bound key
builder between scheduler lookups and worker writes. Mooncake
single-group, Mooncake hybrid, and Memcache lookups now use one call
site while preserving their existing key strings and
all-stage/all-saving-head checks.

- Isolates Mooncake objects by PP stage and requires every PP stage and
saving TP head to be readable before reporting an external cache hit.
- Separates model-global, stage-local, and KV-group-local layer indices
so hybrid cache groups use the correct stage-local ranges and offsets.
- Supports uneven PP partitions, multiple hybrid KV cache groups, and
stage-local MTP/draft cache layers.
- Waits for outstanding PUT operations at the step boundary before
source KV buffers can be reused, including when the final layer has no
save task.
- Builds a stable PP namespace from the topology and resolved KV-group
geometry, avoiding scheduler/worker key mismatches caused by
scheduler-only block-size normalization.
- Avoids mutating the shared DeepSeek-V4 `rope_parameters` while
constructing attention layers. The mutation could change
`ModelConfig.compute_hash()` between the scheduler and PP workers,
causing PUT and lookup operations to use different namespaces and
producing a 0% external cache hit rate.
- Keeps the existing PP=1 Mooncake key format unchanged and rejects
unsupported context parallelism, TP mismatch, recurrent Mamba state, and
PP layouts with empty projected cache groups.

| 模型 | 卡数 | 数据类型 | 是否开 layerwise | 是否池化 | 输入 | 输出 | External prefix
cache | 实际external hit rate | Prefix cache | P并行配置 | D并行配置 | 并发数 | 总请求数
| TTFT/s |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
|DeepseekV4-Flash | 4 | W4A8 | 是 | 是 | 128K | 1 | 90% | 87.44% | / |
DP2PP2 | / | 32 | 128 | 24.4 |
|DeepseekV4-Flash | 4 | W4A8 | 否 | 是 | 128K | 1 | 90% | 87.44% | / |
DP2PP2 | / | 32 | 128 | 24.2 |

Refs #16759

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `AscendStoreConnector` with `backend="mooncake"` and
`use_layerwise=true` now supports topology-matched pipeline parallel
deployments, including uneven PP partitions and hybrid KV cache groups.

No new CLI arguments or environment variables are introduced. The
experimental PP namespace is updated to `mooncake_pp_v3`, so objects
written with the previous PP namespace require a new warm-up write.

### How was this patch tested?

CPU/mock unit tests cover PP=2 and TP=2, uneven stage partitions,
single-group and hybrid multi-group layouts, all-stage hit checks,
missing-stage failures, MTP/draft layers, non-contiguous cache strides,
and final-layer transfer completion.

```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_mooncake_pipeline.py \
  tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_mooncake_hybrid.py \
  tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_mooncake_layerwise.py
```

Result: `41 passed, 4 subtests passed`.

The bound key refactor adds `test_layerwise_keys.py` coverage for both
backends, PP=1/2, single/multiple groups, wire-format compatibility,
layout isolation, frozen configuration, and all-saving-head enumeration.
The related backend, scheduler, worker, and Mooncake tests passed
locally: `292 passed, 207 subtests passed` (2 unrelated KVPP tests
deselected). This CPU/mock run used an A2 build-info stub and a
fail-on-use stub for the unrelated KVPP placement import; it did not
exercise NPU hardware. Changed source files and tests passed targeted
mypy checks for Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 with `--follow-imports skip
--check-untyped-defs --ignore-missing-imports`, plus Ruff, formatting,
compilation, and `git diff --check`. Full `format.sh ci` could not start
locally because pre-commit is not installed.

Real NPU validation of the final external hit rate, generated-token
accuracy, and performance is pending.

commit.message:
[Refactor][RFork] Harden session-managed weight transfer lifecycle (#15935) ### What this PR does / why we need it? This follow-up to #15439 refactors RFork around an explicit session lifecycle and hardens weight reuse across planner, seed, and YuanRong TransferEngine failures. The previous flow spread resource ownership and cleanup across loader, worker, and protocol code, making partial registration, incompatible layouts, transient planner outages, and delayed finalization difficult to recover from. - Introduce `RForkSession` to own planner leases, seed advertisement/heartbeat, registered tensors, transfer promotion, fallback cleanup, and shutdown. - Split RFork configuration, identity/fingerprint, manifest, planner/seed clients, tensor-layout handling, transfer backend, and shared state into focused modules. - Build compatibility fingerprints from model/deployment identity, P/D role, parallel topology, device type, quantization, speculative decoding, model-runner generation, and Ascend weight-layout settings; validate tensor names, shapes, dtypes, NPU formats, logical payloads, and storage/layout metadata before native reads. - Harden YuanRong TransferEngine integration with logical/backing memory registration, bounded registration batches, indexed allocation lookup, an isolated registration cache, serialized lifecycle operations, and bounded retries for `kNotReady` finalization. - Make planner/seed coordination resilient with bounded HTTP requests, lease renewal/expiry, deferred seed promotion, background lease-release retries, seed-health monitoring, and safe model serving when transient remote cleanup or advertisement failures occur. - Update the example planner with lease draining/expiry and allocation behavior, improve RFork load/transfer/layout diagnostics, and document the transfer contracts and new settings. - Add focused unit and integration regression coverage for identity validation, lease release, planner behavior, session/seed-server integration, registration caching, transfer timing, loader fallback, and backend cleanup. ### Refactored architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR Loader["rfork_loader.py
RForkModelLoader"] Fallback["vLLM default loader
safe fallback"] subgraph Runtime["RFork runtime · one RForkSession owns lifecycle"] Session["session.py
RForkSession
state machine + cleanup"] subgraph Core["Identity and validation"] Config["config.py
RForkConfig"] Identity["identity.py
fingerprint + seed key"] Layout["tensor_layout.py
tensor collection + structural digest"] Manifest["manifest.py
pre-read manifest validation"] Types["types.py
states + protocol data"] end subgraph Adapters["Control and data adapters"] PlannerClient["planner_client.py
lease + advertise + heartbeat"] SeedClient["seed_client.py
peer metadata requests"] Transfer["transfer_backend.py
registration + transfer + cleanup"] SeedServer["seed_server.py
local seed HTTP service"] end LocalTE["Local YuanRong TransferEngine
registered NPU buffers"] end Planner["RFork planner
control plane"] subgraph Peer["Existing seed worker"] PeerServer["seed_server.py
metadata + health"] PeerTE["YuanRong TransferEngine
seed weights"] end Loader -->|"creates session and loads model"| Session Loader -.->|"seed miss or unsafe transfer"| Fallback Session -.->|"prepare cleanup before fallback"| Fallback Session --> Config Session --> Identity Session --> Layout Session --> Manifest Session --> PlannerClient Session --> SeedClient Session --> Transfer Session --> SeedServer Session --> Types Identity -->|"compatibility fingerprint"| PlannerClient Layout -->|"structural digest"| PlannerClient PlannerClient -->|"get / renew / release / advertise / heartbeat"| Planner SeedClient -->|"GET transfer metadata"| PeerServer PeerServer -->|"session + manifest"| SeedClient Transfer -->|"register / unregister / finalize"| LocalTE Transfer -->|"remote byte-range reads"| PeerTE ``` The runtime lifecycle is: initialize and register local buffers → acquire a compatible lease → fetch and validate the peer manifest → transfer weights → run post-load processing → start and advertise the local seed service. Seed misses or unsafe transfer failures go through session-owned cleanup before falling back to the default loader; shutdown stops the seed service, releases leases, and finalizes the TransferEngine when all resources are safe to release. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. - RFork rejects incompatible or incomplete seed manifests before native reads and falls back to the default loader when a transfer cannot complete safely. - Transient planner or seed-service failures no longer necessarily interrupt inference. A loaded model can remain available while lease release or seed advertisement retries continue in the background, and seed promotion can be deferred until the source lease is released. - The RFork configuration documentation now covers `rfork_request_timeout_sec`, `rfork_heartbeat_interval_sec`, `rfork_lease_release_max_attempts`, `rfork_lease_release_retry_interval_sec`, `rfork_seed_bind_host`, `rfork_seed_port_base`, and `rfork_seed_advertise_host`. Existing RFork startup arguments remain compatible. - RFork requires a YuanRong TransferEngine release that provides `MemoryRegistration`, `batch_register_memory_ex()`, `ErrorCode.kNotReady`, and `finalize()`. No public vLLM API changes are introduced. ### How was this patch tested? - Added or updated unit and integration coverage under `tests/ut/model_loader/rfork/`, including: - `test_identity_validation.py` - `test_lease_release.py` - `test_registration_cache_isolated.py` - `test_rfork_loader.py` - `test_rfork_planner.py` - `test_session_server_integration.py` - `test_transfer_backend.py` - `test_transfer_timing_isolated.py` - The CI pre-commit failures were caused by Ruff formatting/line length in `config.py` and a forbidden stdlib `re` import in `test_registration_cache_isolated.py`; both are fixed in the amended commits. The latest CI run then reported two mypy type errors in `tensor_layout.py` and `rfork_loader.py`, followed by 13 mypy errors in the RFork test helpers; all are fixed in the current amended commit. The affected Ruff, forbidden-imports, and targeted mypy checks pass locally. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c Signed-off-by: yangsonglin13

[Bugfix][MRV2][P/D] Preserve decode graph with recompute scheduler (#17128)

## Summary

When PD decode uses `recompute_scheduler_enable=true`, the last
prompt-token recompute is reported as prefill by the upstream batch
state. This keeps `has_prefill` true and makes a mixed decode batch miss
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs. Reclassify only the prompt-boundary recompute
on a PD consumer, then refresh `has_prefill` and the uniform decode
token count. This path does not require MTP and does not depend on
#17032.

| Validation | Baseline | Fixed |
|---|---:|---:|
| Targeted UT | — | 4 passed |
| Qwen3-32B-W8A8 requests | 128/128 | 128/128 |
| Aggregate output throughput | 121.84 tok/s | 137.59 tok/s (+12.93%) |
| Mean join decode latency | 3.2335 s | 2.3539 s (-27.20%) |

Full `test_model_runner_v2.py`: 40 passed; its one remaining Spec-PP
failure is also reproducible on the unmodified baseline.

commit.message:
[BugFix][SFA][GLM5Next]Reset positions for dummy batches so sparse backends see a consistent token history (#17170)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`_dummy_run` builds a dummy batch whose `seq_lens` is `max_query_len` (1
for a uniform decode step), but it only resets `self.positions` when
`use_compress` is set:

```python
if self.use_compress:
    self.positions.fill_(127)
    self._dsa_positions_cpu_buf.fill_(127)
```

`use_compress` is derived from whether the model's `hf_config` carries
`compress_ratios`, which marks the DeepSeek V4.x compressed-cache
family. Every other model keeps whatever the previous *real* decode step
wrote into `self.positions`. Attention backends that derive per-token
visibility from positions then plan for a history the dummy sequence
lengths do not describe.

On Ascend A5 with GLM5Next's NoPE sparse MLA this is fatal.
`SparseMLAMetadataState.prepare()` computes per-token top-k lengths from
`positions`, so an idle data-parallel rank produces a plan that claims
~116 visible sparse indices for a sequence the same plan says is 1 token
long. The plan lands in the persistent operator buffer, and the ACL
Graph replay that immediately follows consumes it, which traps inside
`SparseFlashMla`:

```
error code = 341
"The address for VEC to access UB is out of bounds"
```

An ACL Graph replay does not re-enter the module, so the backend's own
`attn_metadata is None` early return cannot intervene: by the time the
graph runs, the inconsistent plan is already in the buffer the graph was
captured
against.

#### Scope

The reset applies only to the backends that read `positions` for
addressing rather than for RoPE:

```python
self.uses_positions_for_attention = self.use_sparse or model_uses_kpool_indexer(
    getattr(vllm_config, "model_config", None)
)
```

`enable_sfa()` returns False for kpool models, so `use_sparse` alone
does not cover GLM-Next. Together the two predicates select exactly the
families whose metadata builders reach
`SparseMLAMetadataState.prepare()`, which calls
`indexer.get_topk_lengths(positions)` - the LightningIndexer SFA family
and the GLM-Next kpool indexer.

Dense and MLA backends derive their addressing from `seq_lens`, the
block table and the slot mapping, all of which a dummy batch already
sets consistently. They consume `positions` only to compute RoPE cos/sin
for a forward whose output is discarded, so they are left untouched.

#### Why this level

Ranks that are idle for the whole request never hit this: their
positions are still 0, so any count derived from them is 1 and agrees
with `seq_lens == 1`. Only a rank that just finished serving carries a
stale history into its first idle step. Resetting positions makes that
rank's dummy step identical to theirs, which is what every backend
already assumes a dummy batch looks like.

Fixing it inside one backend would leave the same trap for the next
backend that reads positions, which is why it belongs in `_dummy_run`
next to the existing `use_compress` reset rather than in the SFA
metadata builder.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

Ascend A5, GLM5Next w8a8, ACL Graph enabled.

- DP4 / TP2 / EP8, one request with `max_tokens=100` and nothing sent
afterwards: without this patch the request returns HTTP 200 with correct
output and the service then traps with `error code = 341` in
`SparseFlashMla` while idle; with it the idle step is survived and the
failure signature is gone.
- DP8 / TP1 / EP8 with MTP (5 speculative steps), `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`:
the server starts and gsm8k completes with accuracy in the expected
range. This exercises the multi-token dummy batch
(`uniform_decode_query_len == 6`), where every dummy token reports
position 0 while its sequence length is 6 - an under-statement that
keeps `ori_topk_length <= seqused_ori_kv`, which the operator contract
requires.
- `--enforce-eager` does not reproduce it:
`_should_build_dummy_attn_metadata()` is only true for `force_attention`
or
`CUDAGraphMode.FULL`, so the reset path is not reached and no metadata
is built from the stale positions. Configurations without data
parallelism do not reproduce it either, because they have no idle dummy
batches.

[Performance][DSA]Cache group-invariant metadata in build_req_metadata (#17153)

<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!

BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ
https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing/overview.html

-->
### What this PR does / why we need it?
<!--
- Please clarify what changes you are proposing. The purpose of this
section is to outline the changes and how this PR fixes the issue.
If possible, please consider writing useful notes for better and faster
reviews in your PR.

- Please clarify why the changes are needed. For instance, the use case
and bug description.

- Fixes #
-->
This PR optimizes `build_req_metadata` in
`vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py` by caching group-invariant metadata
(`req_preamble`) in `metadata_cache`. Since `build()` runs once per
`(kv_cache_group, attn_group)` pair but receives the same
`query_start_loc` and `seq_lens` objects, computing these values once on
the first group and sharing them avoids redundant computations.
Additionally, `start_pos_prefill` is updated by copying the shared
`start_pos` and zeroing out only the tail past `num_reqs` to maintain
capture-stable addresses.
```
execute_model                      (worker/model_runner_v1.py)
  └─ _build_attention_metadata
       │
       common_ratio_to_sas_metadata = {}
       for kv_cache_gid, kv_cache_group in enumerate(
               self.kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups): 
           cm = copy(cm_base) 
           if kv_cache_gid > 0:
               cm.block_table_tensor, cm.slot_mapping = ... 
           for attn_gid in range(len(self.attn_groups[kv_cache_gid])):
               _build_attn_group_metadata(...)
                 └─ builder.build()
                      └─ attention/dsa_v1.py  build_req_metadata()   ← eight times
```

| backend | layers[0] |
|---|---|
| `AscendDSAC4Backend` | `...self_attn.indexer.k_cache` |
| `AscendDSAC4Backend` | `...self_attn.attn` |
| `AscendDSAC128Backend` | `...self_attn.attn` |
| `AscendDSASWABackend` | `...self_attn.swa_cache` |
| `AscendDSASWABackend` | `...self_attn.swa_cache` |
| `AscendDSAC4StateBackend` | `...compressor.state_cache` |
| `AscendDSAC4StateBackend` | `...indexer.compressor.state_cache` |
| `AscendDSAC128StateBackend` | `...compressor.state_cache` |

```python
num_reqs = common_attn_metadata.num_reqs
query_start_loc     = common_attn_metadata.query_start_loc[: num_reqs + 1]
query_start_loc_cpu = common_attn_metadata.query_start_loc_cpu[: num_reqs + 1]
seq_lens   = self.seq_lens[:num_reqs]
seq_lens_q = query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]
max_seqlen_q  = torch.max(query_start_loc_cpu[1:] - query_start_loc_cpu[:-1]).item()
max_seqlen_kv = torch.max(seq_lens_cpu[:num_reqs]).item()
...
self.start_pos_prefill.fill_(0)
self.start_pos_prefill[:num_reqs] = seq_lens - seq_lens_q
```
```
sub, sub, max, fill_, item, max, fill_, item, fill_, sub, copy_
```
Following the existing pattern in build(), fold the three
group-invariant quantities into common_ratio_to_sas_metadata, gated by a
separate req_preamble key.

Note that it means *any* user-facing change including all aspects such
as API, interface or other behavior changes.
Documentation-only updates are not considered user-facing changes.
-->
no

[CI] Refresh estimated test times from recent E2E timing data (rebase of #16909) (#17230)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Refreshes `estimated_times.yaml` with measured values from the scheduled
full-E2E timing run (source run 35342381487, data collected
2026-09-17/18),
re-applying the refresh from bot PR #16909 onto current main (which was
CONFLICTING because of newer main commits).

- **105 entries** updated to measured medians (x1.1 safety buffer,
rounded to 10s).
  Largest corrections (old -> new):
  - `four_card/model_runner_v2/test_deepseek_v4.py`: 520 -> 2190
  - `two_card/spec_decode/test_spec_decode.py`: 690 -> 1870
  - `four_card/test_sequence_parallel_linear.py`: 340 -> 1190
  - `four_card/context_parallel/test_deepseek_v4.py`: 520 -> 1230
  - `one_card/lora/test_qwenvl_lora.py`: 600 -> 1230
  - and 100 more smaller corrections (both up and down)
- **5 entries intentionally skipped** where main already has newer
values:
- `test_qwen3_next.py` / `test_cpu_weight_offload.py` /
`test_shared_expert_dp.py`:
#16701 (9/22) optimized these test durations and set fresh estimates;
the
    9/18 measurements predate the optimization and would regress them.
  - `test_npu_ipc_weight_transfer.py` / `test_hccl_weight_transfer.py`:
#16959 restructured these tests into `rlhf/state_transitions/` with new
    three-model cases; old-path measurements no longer apply.

Accurate estimates keep `select_tests.py` LPT shard balancing even and
reduce
the CI critical path (the stale low estimates for deepseek_v4 /

commit.message:
[Feature][KV Transfer] Add D2RH host cache with local HBM prefix hits (#15912)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

- Add `MooncakeD2RHConnectorV1`, retaining D-side Host staging/cache
while reusing local HBM prefixes.
- Keep the existing opt-in partial-group prefix lookup for DeepSeek-V4
remote-prefill consumers (`D2RH_EXTERNAL_PARTIAL_PREFIX_CACHE=1`).
- Refresh the model block size at Mooncake scheduler initialization,
before snapshotting it. Resolve the DSV4 transfer block size from its
sliding-window MLA spec, rather than the hybrid allocator quantum or the
largest state-cache spec.
- Remove the late D2RH `request_finished` block-size rewrite: the
scheduler must use consistent geometry throughout the request lifecycle,
not just in its final response.
- Add connector scheduler regression tests and focused D2RH PP
mapping/component/lifetime tests. No new per-request INFO logging is
introduced by these updates.

Hybrid cache initialization can replace the logical DSV4 block size with
a smaller physical allocation quantum. Using that value for connector
metadata/hash indexing loses valid D-side HBM prefix hits. The
initialization fix aligns scheduler metadata with the worker's logical
KV layout.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes: an opt-in D2RH connector with Host-cache reuse, local-HBM prefix
reuse, and prefill-PP transfer support. This PR does not modify the
example proxy or add a rank-affinity option. Routing policy is outside
its scope.

The normal D2RH path retains the D Host cache. The diagnostic benchmark
that skipped P/KV handoff is not the production implementation and is
not included in this PR.

## How was this patch tested?

### Historical targeted tests before proxy separation

- Repository-pinned Ruff **0.14.0** check and format check on the
changed Python files: passed.
- Static compilation of the changed Python files: passed.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` was attempted but stopped while initializing
the Markdown hook's dependencies on Windows; the complete all-files hook
suite is **not** reported as passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- In an isolated source tree on the A5 day20260904 container, the
Mooncake connector + proxy test files: **140 passed, 1 failed**. The
sole failure is the existing
`TestKVCacheRecvingThreadBasic::test_submit_request_serializes_same_peer_fifo`
one-second thread-start wait. The same test also fails on the unchanged
PR head `09a366ef477337d6caa01ddf49ad35a557ee3ed6` in the same
environment. It is not reported as a green full suite.
- `tests/ut/test_compressed_prefix_cache.py`: **12 passed**.
- At that earlier revision, the scheduler and proxy tests reported **16
passed** (125 unrelated tests deselected). The proxy-specific tests have
since been removed with the proxy change; this is a historical result,
not the current test count. Existing review threads are not
automatically marked resolved.

### Recorded hardware validation of the runtime fixes now ported into
this update

Image:
`vllm-ascend:dev-26.2.0.day20260904-A5-py311-Ubuntu24.04-lts-aarch64`;
model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash. P and D each use DP4/TP1 (four NPUs each),
both prefix caches enabled, CPU binding disabled, MTP=1. D uses the
recompute scheduler. Normal PD benchmarks use matching-rank routing.
These are previously completed runtime measurements using an
experiment-specific matching-rank proxy, not a fresh performance run of
the final PR commit with the unmodified example proxy. That routing
modification is no longer included in this PR.

Prefill-oriented case: 128K input, 1 output token, 98% repeated prefix,
concurrency 32, 320 requests.

- PD proxy: **3.5694 req/s**; direct P: **3.4910 req/s** (PD +2.25%).
- Both: **320/320 successful**, zero failures, identical actual
input-length distributions, all outputs exactly 1 token.
- Actual P/D local prefix hit rates for PD: approximately **96.87%**.
Dataset repetition is not the same as measured cache hit rate.

Decode-oriented case: 128K input, 1024 output tokens, 100% repeated
data, concurrency 40, 320 requests.

- PD proxy: **2087.7728 output token/s**, average TTFT **3638.1 ms**,
average end-to-end **18823.9 ms**.
- Direct D (mixed/prefill+decode path): **2167.4741 output token/s**,
average TTFT **1589.2 ms**, average end-to-end **18445.4 ms**.
- PD output throughput is **3.68% lower**, not identical. Both:
**320/320 successful**, all outputs exactly 1024 tokens, no D
preemptions.
- D local prefix hit rate: **99.996948%** (131072/131076). P still
computes approximately 4100 prompt tokens/request; it is not a P-side
100%-hit test.
- D2RH Host-cache logs show hits=304/misses=0 per formal PD request.
This is not proof that every hybrid KV group needs zero H2D traffic; no
isolated H2D-byte/timing measurement is claimed.

At concurrency 32, the earlier PD result was 1568.9433 output token/s,
but a same-configuration recheck reached 1880.9528 without production
code changes. Consequently, the earlier approximately 20% gap is not
presented as a fixed connector transfer penalty. Runs are not a
randomized multi-repeat significance study, and overall throughput
comparisons do not imply equal per-NPU efficiency (PD uses eight NPUs,
direct P/D four).

The prior description's unconditional “formal Host-to-HBM transfers: 0”
statement has been removed: the new-image validation supports local-HBM
and Host-cache reuse, not a universal zero-H2D claim. Production
services were not replaced/restarted while preparing this PR update.

## Proxy separated from this PR

The example proxy is restored exactly to the PR base, and
`tests/ut/examples/test_pd_proxy_rank_affinity.py` is removed. D2RH
Host/HBM cache and PP connector changes remain unchanged. The removal
received Ruff 0.14.0 check/format, Python compilation, base-file
equality, and diff-whitespace checks. The complete format hook suite
remains unverified because Markdown environment installation hangs.
Running services and the experiment proxy were not modified or
restarted. No new accuracy or performance claim for disabling rank
affinity is made.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

commit.message:
[BugFix][Sleep Mode] Register level-2 runtime tensors as non-persistent buffers (#16725)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Part of the sleep-mode tensor-ownership work in #16558 (the Ascend
counterpart of vllm-project/vllm#53343), and the same bug class fixed
upstream by vllm-project/vllm#53507 for CUDA models.

`NPUWorker.load_model()` wraps `model_runner.load_model()` in
`CaMemAllocator.use_memory_pool(tag="weights")`, so model construction,
`load_weights` and `process_weights_after_loading` all allocate in that
pool. At level 2 `CaMemAllocator.sleep()` releases every allocation of
the pool without a CPU backup, and `NPUWorker.wake_up()` restores
contents only for `model.named_buffers()`. A runtime tensor created in
that scope that is stored in a plain attribute -- or owned by a helper
that is not an `nn.Module`, or held only in a module-level global --
therefore comes back pointing at remapped, empty storage. When the code
that would recreate it is guarded by `... is None`, the Python reference
survives the sleep, the guard is never true again, and the forward path
silently reads discarded memory (a captured ACL graph keeps a valid
device pointer and reads garbage).

This PR registers the affected tensors as non-persistent model buffers,
the pattern already used in this repo for `_dsa_hadamard` (#13352),
`expert_ids_per_ep_rank`, the EPLB state and the GLM-Next KPool indexer
weights, and by upstream in vllm-project/vllm#53507. `persistent=False`
keeps runtime-derived state out of checkpoints, and the buffer objects
keep their device addresses, so arguments captured by ACL graphs stay
valid.

Four sites were found inside the `weights` scope:

1. `vllm_ascend/attention/indexer.py` -- `AscendSFAIndexerBackend` kept
the LI C8 Hadamard matrices (`q_hadamard`, `k_hadamard`) as **class
attributes** and rebuilt them only while they were `None`. They are read
by every SFA indexer forward (`forward_k`, `forward_q`), so a level-2
wake corrupted the indexer input of every layer. They are now
per-instance non-persistent buffers, filled once per layer by
`process_weights_after_loading()` and kept as the same tensors across
reloads.
2. `vllm_ascend/attention/context_parallel/sfa_cp.py` --
`AscendSFADCPImpl.__init__` builds the DCP sparse-index remap order
(`_remap_order`) and its sentinel (`_remap_invalid_index`), which are
read by `_remap_sparse_indices` on the non-Triton fallback path. The
impl is not an `nn.Module`, so they are now published as non-persistent
buffers of the owning attention module (same owner lookup as
`get_or_register_attention_buffer`, with a fallback to the `o_proj`
module when an integration does not forward `layer_name`).
3. `vllm_ascend/ops/rope_dsv4.py` -- `ComplexExpRotaryEmbedding`
precomputes the DeepSeek-V4 DSA RoPE tables into the process-global
`_ROPE_STATE.full_rope_cache` and rebuilds them only for a config key it
has not seen. Every DSA layer reads those tables (`get_cos_and_sin_dsa`,
`get_full_cos_and_sin_dsa`), so after a level-2 wake all RoPE tables
were corrupted. The cached tensors are now also registered as
non-persistent buffers of the module that built them; the global cache
keeps the same objects, so the lookup path and the addresses baked into
captured ACL graphs are unchanged, and `named_buffers()` de-duplicates
the tables shared by layers with the same config key.
4. `vllm_ascend/ops/rotary_embedding.py` --
`_record_cos_and_sin_cache_interleaved()` derives the de-interleaved
cos/sin tables that every MLA/SFA rope lookup reads through the module
globals `_cos_cache`/`_sin_cache` (`get_cos_and_sin_mla`, used by
`sfa_v1.py`, `mla_v1.py` and `indexer.py`), but held them only in those
globals. `cos_sin_cache` itself is a non-persistent buffer and survived
the wake; the derived pair did not, so every MLA/SFA layer applied
identity RoPE afterwards while all pointers stayed valid. The pair is
now registered as non-persistent buffers of the module that built it,
with the globals keeping the very same tensor objects.

Site 4 is what the same-chip lane of the GLM-5.1 live weight-update test
was missing, which is why that case was skipped before. With it fixed,
`test_npu_ipc_weight_transfer.py` reproduces a normal startup load of
the payload exactly, so the GLM-5.1 `skip_reason` is removed from
`tests/e2e/pull_request/rlhf/weight_transfer_test_utils.py` and the case
now runs in both lanes. The other stated blocker ("the SFA
runtime-weight refresh is still pending") turned out not to apply: the
state that *is* weight-derived (the KPool indexer's FP32
`_wk`/`_gate`/`_norm` copies, SFA's `W_UK_T`/`W_UV`) is re-derived by
the layerwise reload, which finalizes deferred attention layers through
`process_weights_after_loading` -- the never-sleeping lanes reproduce
the reference exactly without any extra refresh hook.

Scope of the audit, so reviewers can see what was checked and
deliberately left alone:

- Only allocations made inside a `use_memory_pool` context are tracked
by `CaMemAllocator`, so tensors created during the first forward /
runner init and all metadata-builder state (built by
`initialize_attn_backend`, which runs outside the narrowed `kv_cache`
pool) survive sleep and are not part of this bug class.
- The audit was also run over **module-level tensor globals** under
`vllm_ascend` by dumping each one's digest (shape, dtype, sum, sampled
values) plus whether the model actually owns the object before and after
a level-2 wake. That is how site 4 was found; the same sweep now reports
no other unowned, content-losing global in the GLM-5.1 configuration.
- Derived weights created by `process_weights_after_loading`
(MLA/SFA/MLAPO preprocessed weights, quantization methods, `*_list` /
fused-scale MoE views) are rebuilt by the layerwise reload path
(`reload_weights` re-runs `process_weights_after_loading`), so they
recover their values; keeping their addresses stable is the separate
concern already handled for `W_UV`/`W_UK_T`.
- Scratch state that is fully rewritten before each read
(`expert_token_nums`, `topk_indices_buffer`, `per_layer_embeddings`,
`_mtp_hidden_buffer`, RoPE runtime buffers, sparse-KV-offload selection
state, `alibi_slopes`, the zero-element `sfa_qsfa_kr_cache_dummy`) is
discardable by contract and is intentionally left as a plain attribute.
- Two findings are **not** fixed here and deserve follow-ups:
`AscendEplbLayerState.expert_replica_routing_table` (EPLB refresh path;
needs runtime verification), and
`Glm5NextLinearAttention._merged_conv_weight` (built on the first
forward, so it survives sleep but stays stale after a level-2 reload
because nothing invalidates its `is None` guard).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. The tensors are still created and consumed exactly as before; they
are additionally registered as non-persistent buffers, so they stay out
of `state_dict()`/checkpoints and non-sleep-mode runs are unaffected.
The observable differences are correct contents after a level-2 wake and
a small amount of extra buffer bookkeeping.

### How was this patch tested?

Added `tests/ut/test_sleep_mode_tensor_ownership.py`, which pins the
contract instead of a single call site:

- the tensors the forward paths read (the LI C8 Hadamard matrices, the
DCP remap order/sentinel, the DeepSeek-V4 DSA RoPE tables and the

[BugFix][Sleep Mode] Register level-2 runtime tensors as non-persistent buffers (#16725)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Part of the sleep-mode tensor-ownership work in #16558 (the Ascend
counterpart of vllm-project/vllm#53343), and the same bug class fixed
upstream by vllm-project/vllm#53507 for CUDA models.

`NPUWorker.load_model()` wraps `model_runner.load_model()` in
`CaMemAllocator.use_memory_pool(tag="weights")`, so model construction,
`load_weights` and `process_weights_after_loading` all allocate in that
pool. At level 2 `CaMemAllocator.sleep()` releases every allocation of
the pool without a CPU backup, and `NPUWorker.wake_up()` restores
contents only for `model.named_buffers()`. A runtime tensor created in
that scope that is stored in a plain attribute -- or owned by a helper
that is not an `nn.Module`, or held only in a module-level global --
therefore comes back pointing at remapped, empty storage. When the code
that would recreate it is guarded by `... is None`, the Python reference
survives the sleep, the guard is never true again, and the forward path
silently reads discarded memory (a captured ACL graph keeps a valid
device pointer and reads garbage).

This PR registers the affected tensors as non-persistent model buffers,
the pattern already used in this repo for `_dsa_hadamard` (#13352),
`expert_ids_per_ep_rank`, the EPLB state and the GLM-Next KPool indexer
weights, and by upstream in vllm-project/vllm#53507. `persistent=False`
keeps runtime-derived state out of checkpoints, and the buffer objects
keep their device addresses, so arguments captured by ACL graphs stay
valid.

Four sites were found inside the `weights` scope:

1. `vllm_ascend/attention/indexer.py` -- `AscendSFAIndexerBackend` kept
the LI C8 Hadamard matrices (`q_hadamard`, `k_hadamard`) as **class
attributes** and rebuilt them only while they were `None`. They are read
by every SFA indexer forward (`forward_k`, `forward_q`), so a level-2
wake corrupted the indexer input of every layer. They are now
per-instance non-persistent buffers, filled once per layer by
`process_weights_after_loading()` and kept as the same tensors across
reloads.
2. `vllm_ascend/attention/context_parallel/sfa_cp.py` --
`AscendSFADCPImpl.__init__` builds the DCP sparse-index remap order
(`_remap_order`) and its sentinel (`_remap_invalid_index`), which are
read by `_remap_sparse_indices` on the non-Triton fallback path. The
impl is not an `nn.Module`, so they are now published as non-persistent
buffers of the owning attention module (same owner lookup as
`get_or_register_attention_buffer`, with a fallback to the `o_proj`
module when an integration does not forward `layer_name`).
3. `vllm_ascend/ops/rope_dsv4.py` -- `ComplexExpRotaryEmbedding`
precomputes the DeepSeek-V4 DSA RoPE tables into the process-global
`_ROPE_STATE.full_rope_cache` and rebuilds them only for a config key it
has not seen. Every DSA layer reads those tables (`get_cos_and_sin_dsa`,
`get_full_cos_and_sin_dsa`), so after a level-2 wake all RoPE tables
were corrupted. The cached tensors are now also registered as
non-persistent buffers of the module that built them; the global cache
keeps the same objects, so the lookup path and the addresses baked into
captured ACL graphs are unchanged, and `named_buffers()` de-duplicates
the tables shared by layers with the same config key.
4. `vllm_ascend/ops/rotary_embedding.py` --
`_record_cos_and_sin_cache_interleaved()` derives the de-interleaved
cos/sin tables that every MLA/SFA rope lookup reads through the module
globals `_cos_cache`/`_sin_cache` (`get_cos_and_sin_mla`, used by
`sfa_v1.py`, `mla_v1.py` and `indexer.py`), but held them only in those
globals. `cos_sin_cache` itself is a non-persistent buffer and survived
the wake; the derived pair did not, so every MLA/SFA layer applied
identity RoPE afterwards while all pointers stayed valid. The pair is
now registered as non-persistent buffers of the module that built it,
with the globals keeping the very same tensor objects.

Site 4 is what the same-chip lane of the GLM-5.1 live weight-update test
was missing, which is why that case was skipped before. With it fixed,
`test_npu_ipc_weight_transfer.py` reproduces a normal startup load of
the payload exactly, so the GLM-5.1 `skip_reason` is removed from
`tests/e2e/pull_request/rlhf/weight_transfer_test_utils.py` and the case
now runs in both lanes. The other stated blocker ("the SFA
runtime-weight refresh is still pending") turned out not to apply: the
state that *is* weight-derived (the KPool indexer's FP32
`_wk`/`_gate`/`_norm` copies, SFA's `W_UK_T`/`W_UV`) is re-derived by
the layerwise reload, which finalizes deferred attention layers through
`process_weights_after_loading` -- the never-sleeping lanes reproduce
the reference exactly without any extra refresh hook.

Scope of the audit, so reviewers can see what was checked and
deliberately left alone:

- Only allocations made inside a `use_memory_pool` context are tracked
by `CaMemAllocator`, so tensors created during the first forward /
runner init and all metadata-builder state (built by
`initialize_attn_backend`, which runs outside the narrowed `kv_cache`
pool) survive sleep and are not part of this bug class.
- The audit was also run over **module-level tensor globals** under
`vllm_ascend` by dumping each one's digest (shape, dtype, sum, sampled
values) plus whether the model actually owns the object before and after
a level-2 wake. That is how site 4 was found; the same sweep now reports
no other unowned, content-losing global in the GLM-5.1 configuration.
- Derived weights created by `process_weights_after_loading`
(MLA/SFA/MLAPO preprocessed weights, quantization methods, `*_list` /
fused-scale MoE views) are rebuilt by the layerwise reload path
(`reload_weights` re-runs `process_weights_after_loading`), so they
recover their values; keeping their addresses stable is the separate
concern already handled for `W_UV`/`W_UK_T`.
- Scratch state that is fully rewritten before each read
(`expert_token_nums`, `topk_indices_buffer`, `per_layer_embeddings`,
`_mtp_hidden_buffer`, RoPE runtime buffers, sparse-KV-offload selection
state, `alibi_slopes`, the zero-element `sfa_qsfa_kr_cache_dummy`) is
discardable by contract and is intentionally left as a plain attribute.
- Two findings are **not** fixed here and deserve follow-ups:
`AscendEplbLayerState.expert_replica_routing_table` (EPLB refresh path;
needs runtime verification), and
`Glm5NextLinearAttention._merged_conv_weight` (built on the first
forward, so it survives sleep but stays stale after a level-2 reload
because nothing invalidates its `is None` guard).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. The tensors are still created and consumed exactly as before; they
are additionally registered as non-persistent buffers, so they stay out
of `state_dict()`/checkpoints and non-sleep-mode runs are unaffected.
The observable differences are correct contents after a level-2 wake and
a small amount of extra buffer bookkeeping.

[Bugfix][Engram] Guard config patch when upstream Engram is unavailable (#17243)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix the nightly startup regression introduced by #17134. vLLM builds
without `vllm.config.engram` fail during platform patch import,
including non-Engram models. Restore the module availability guard
around the Engram patch.

Reported failure:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35706225123/job/106677606559

Restores startup on vLLM builds without Engram. Existing Engram
configuration behavior is unchanged.

- Reproduced the original import failure on installed vLLM `752a3a5044`;
the guarded patch now loads as a no-op.

`84030bbe`: 9 passed.
- Ruff and diff checks passed. Local `format.sh ci` is blocked by the
missing `pre_commit` Python package.

[BugFix][Spec Decode] Restore DSpARK weight post-processing on MRV1 (#17258)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

#16347 moved Qwen3 DSpARK rotation alignment from `load_weights()` into
`post_process()`, but only MRV2 invokes the new hook. MRV1 consequently
loads the draft without aligning its projection with a rotated target.

Call the optional DSpARK `post_process()` hook with the target
configuration after embedding/lm_head sharing and before draft
hidden-state precomputation. This preserves the final aligned weights
and ensures precomputed hidden states use the updated projection.

The GLM-5.2 W4A8 DSpARK nightly on main `baa023ada` reported
first-position acceptance of 8.46% against an 84.55% minimum while GSM8K
accuracy remained 96.44%:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35631828275/job/106484161637.
The missing MRV1 hook is confirmed in that revision; acceptance recovery
still needs the nightly rerun.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Restores DSpARK draft post-processing on MRV1. No new configuration
options.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added three regression cases to
`tests/ut/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer.py`, covering hook
ordering, target configuration, precomputed hidden states, a draft
without the hook, and the non-DSpARK path.
- Executed those repository tests against the actual `load_model()`
method in an isolated CPU harness: before the fix, 1 failed / 2 passed;
after the fix, 3 passed.
- Ruff check/format and `git diff --check` passed.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c
